questions.q: How does TOGAF fundamentally treat the enterprise for the purpose of architecture?
o: As a system whose components, relationships, and evolution can be architected
questions.e: TOGAF treats the enterprise as a system. Architecture concerns the components, their interrelationships, and the principles governing their design and evolution over time.

questions.q: Which statement supports why TOGAF is suitable as an EA framework?
o: It is a rigid method that cannot be tailored
It is generic, best-practice, and must be tailored, and can integrate with frameworks like ITIL, COBIT, and PRINCE2
It only works for government agencies
It mandates a single vendor toolset
questions.e: TOGAF is a generic, community-developed, best-practice framework that must be tailored and can be used standalone or integrated with ITIL, COBIT, or PRINCE2.

questions.q: The Business Architecture domain describes which of the following?
o: Business strategy, governance, organization, and key business processes
The structure of physical data assets
questions.e: The Business Architecture describes business strategy, governance, organization, and key processes, including capabilities, value streams, org units, and information concepts.

questions.q: Which of the following does the Solutions Continuum structure?
o: Solution building blocks that support and realize the architectures
questions.e: The Solutions Continuum structures solution building blocks that implement the architectures, complementing the Architecture Continuum which structures ABBs.

questions.q: Which part of the Architecture Repository records decision logs, compliance assessments, and capability assessments?
questions.e: The Governance Repository records governance activity: decision logs, compliance assessments, and capability assessments.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly orders the risk management activities in TOGAF?
o: Identify, classify, initial assessment, mitigation, residual assessment, monitoring
Classify, identify, initial assessment, mitigation, residual assessment, monitoring
questions.e: The six activities in order are: risk classification, risk identification, initial risk assessment, risk mitigation and residual risk assessment, then risk monitoring and governance. Classification comes first, before identification.

questions.q: In the gap analysis matrix, how are the baseline and target ABBs arranged?
o: Target ABBs on the vertical axis, baseline ABBs on the horizontal axis
Target ABBs on the horizontal axis, baseline ABBs on the vertical axis
Baseline and target are not shown in the same matrix
questions.e: Target ABBs are listed on the horizontal axis and baseline ABBs on the vertical axis, with a 'new' row and an 'eliminated' column added.

questions.q: How does TOGAF define a Transition Architecture?
o: The current-state reference for all changes
An intermediate, fully functional state that partially realizes the target and delivers benefits
The state where all change activity is suspended
questions.e: A Transition Architecture is an intermediate, fully functional future state that partially realizes the target and already provides benefits; used when a direct jump is risky.

questions.q: Among the five architecture states, which one always exists?
questions.e: There is always a baseline (the current state, the reference for all changes), but not necessarily a target, transition, candidate, or resting architecture.

questions.q: Which of the following is an output of the Preliminary Phase?
o: Organizational Model, Tailored Framework, and Architecture Principles
questions.e: The Preliminary Phase produces the Organizational Model for EA, the Tailored Architecture Framework, Architecture Principles, and the initial Request for Architecture Work.

questions.q: Which technique is primarily used in Phases A and B to identify and understand business needs and derive requirements?
questions.e: Business scenarios are used mainly in Phases A and B to identify and understand business needs and derive the requirements the architecture must address.

questions.q: Which artifact is a typical Technology Architecture output in Phase D?
questions.e: The Technology Portfolio Catalog lists all technology in use and is a Phase D artifact, alongside the Platform Decomposition Diagram and Environments and Locations Diagram.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a work package on the Architecture Roadmap?
o: A unit of work with a description, dependencies, business value, and links to the ADD and requirements
questions.e: A work package has a description, dependencies, assigned business value, and links to the ADD and requirements; the roadmap consolidates work packages and Transition Architectures.

questions.q: Which deliverables are both finalized in Phase F?
o: Architecture Definition Document and Architecture Requirements Specification
Request for Architecture Work and Statement of Architecture Work
questions.e: Both the ADD and the Architecture Requirements Specification are finalized in Phase F, along with the detailed Implementation and Migration Plan and the Architecture Roadmap.

questions.q: How does the Architecture Compliance Assessment support Phase G?
o: It triggers a new ADM cycle automatically
It ensures the realized implementation aligns with strategic and architectural objectives and validates that requirements are followed
questions.e: The Architecture Compliance Assessment ensures the realized design and implementation align with the architectural objectives and vision; used in Phase G to validate requirements are followed and in Phase H to assess realized value.

questions.q: Phase H is often described as a 'holding phase'. What does this mean?
o: It keeps the ADM running while monitoring change and deciding whether to update or start a new cycle
It holds the budget for all projects
It stores all deliverables in the repository
questions.e: Phase H is a holding phase that keeps the ADM running; it manages change and decides whether a Change Request warrants a light update or a new ADM cycle.

questions.q: In step 6 of ADM Requirements Management, which statement about handling changed requirements is correct?
o: Requirements Management alone assesses impacts and decides implementation or deferral
The relevant ADM phase assesses impacts on current and previous phases, decides implementation or deferral, and issues Requirements Impact Assessment version n+1
The updated impact assessment replaces the Architecture Vision
Only the Preliminary Phase evaluates changed requirements
questions.e: Step 6 assigns impact assessment, the implementation-or-deferral decision, and issue of Requirements Impact Assessment version n+1 to the relevant ADM phase. Step 5 separately assigns generation of an impact assessment to Requirements Management.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes architecture principles?
o: Detailed technical specifications for a single project
Enduring general rules and guidelines, seldom amended, forming the basis for architecture decisions
The measurable success criteria of an implementation
questions.e: Architecture principles are enduring general rules and guidelines, seldom amended, that form the basis for future architecture decisions and set precedence in trade-offs.

questions.q: Which is the correct set of four sections in the TOGAF Architecture Principles template?
questions.e: The four sections are Name, Statement, Rationale, and Implications.

questions.q: A principle whose intentions are clear and unambiguous, minimizing violations, satisfies which criterion?
questions.e: Understandable means the principle's intentions are clear and unambiguous so that violations are minimized. The five criteria are Complete, Consistent, Stable, Understandable, Robust.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of gap analysis as an ADM technique?
o: To assign business value to work packages
To highlight shortfalls between the Baseline and Target Architectures
questions.e: Gap analysis highlights shortfalls between the Baseline and Target Architectures, including items deliberately omitted, accidentally left out, or not yet defined.

questions.q: According to TOGAF, which dimension is the most important in a Business Transformation Readiness Assessment?
questions.e: The human factor is the most important dimension of the BTRA; a change-averse culture can undermine even the best plan.

questions.q: In the TOGAF risk classification scheme, which pair describes the effect and frequency axes?
questions.e: Effect is rated catastrophic, critical, marginal, or negligible; frequency is frequent, likely, occasional, seldom, or unlikely. These combine into impact levels E, H, M, L.

questions.q: Which fundamental content documents of the TOGAF Standard are dedicated to the ADM?
o: The ADM, ADM Techniques, and Applying the ADM documents
questions.e: Three of the six fundamental content documents are dedicated to the ADM: the ADM, ADM Techniques, and Applying the ADM, reflecting that the ADM is the heart of the standard.

questions.q: In TOGAF 10, what is a defining feature of a digital enterprise?
o: It creates fully digital products/services or delivers physical products/services by digital means
questions.e: A digital enterprise creates fully digital products and services or delivers physical products and services by digital means; addressed by Series Guide G217.

questions.q: Which Landscape level typically supports program and portfolio roadmaps at a medium level of detail and breadth?
questions.e: The Segment level has medium breadth, detail, and time horizon, and supports program and portfolio roadmaps. Multiple segment architectures cover the strategic area at more detail.

questions.q: Which statement about the architecture partitioning model is correct?
o: TOGAF defines one definitive partitioning model for all enterprises
There is no single definitive model; it should reflect the enterprise's operating model
Partitioning must always match the org chart
Partitioning is only allowed at the capability level
questions.e: There is no single definitive partitioning model; the model should reflect the enterprise's operating model, and each partition has one owning team.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes abstraction levels from Landscape levels?
o: Abstraction levels are contextual/conceptual/logical/physical (perspective); Landscape levels are strategic/segment/capability (granularity)
questions.e: Abstraction levels (contextual, conceptual, logical, physical) are about perspective; Landscape levels (strategic, segment, capability) are about granularity. Do not confuse them.

questions.q: Governance is best defined in TOGAF as which of the following?
o: A system by which the current and future state are directed and controlled
A one-time approval by the sponsor
The act of writing implementation code
The selection of a technology vendor
questions.e: Governance is a system by which the current and future state are directed and controlled; it is a hierarchical, committed decision-making process.

questions.q: Which of the following is a stated goal of the Architecture Board?
o: To write the enterprise business strategy
To ensure consistency of sub-architectures, set reuse targets, and provide an escalation capability
questions.e: Architecture Board goals include improving EA maturity, ensuring architecture-based development is adopted, ensuring consistency of sub-architectures, enforcing compliance, setting reuse targets, and providing escalation.

questions.q: The Architecture Design and Development Contract is an agreement with which parties?
o: System integrators and application providers (development partners)
questions.e: The Architecture Design and Development Contract is a statement of intent to design and develop the EA, made with development partners such as system integrators and application providers.

questions.q: Which of the following describes the enterprise and IT governance function of architecture compliance?
o: It informs projects how the EA impacts them
It defines a formal compliance review process for reviewing project compliance to the target EA
questions.e: The enterprise and IT governance function of architecture compliance defines the formal compliance review process for reviewing project compliance to the target EA.

questions.q: Which statement about the relationship between a view and a viewpoint is correct?
o: A view exists independently of any viewpoint
Every view is rooted in a viewpoint, which governs the structure and content of the view
A viewpoint is a specific instance of a view
questions.e: Every view has an associated viewpoint; the viewpoint is the generic, reusable lens that governs the structure and content of the specific view built for stakeholders.

questions.q: In TOGAF, how is a stakeholder defined?
o: Only a paying customer of the enterprise
An individual, team, organization, or class thereof having an interest in a system
questions.e: A stakeholder is an individual, team, organization, or class thereof having an interest in a system; in EA the system is the enterprise or part of it.

questions.q: Which correctly pairs an ABB and an SBB using the video-conferencing example?
o: ABB = 'Video Conferencing Services' (the capability); SBB = a specific product such as WebEx or Teams plus servers
questions.e: The ABB is the logical, supplier-independent capability ('Video Conferencing Services'); the SBB is the physical implementation, such as WebEx or Teams with servers and network.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the Implementation and Migration Plan?
o: To show the aspirational vision of the end product
To provide a schedule of projects that realizes the target, showing the 'how' of the transformation
To trigger the start of an ADM cycle
questions.e: The Implementation and Migration Plan is a schedule of projects toward the target, showing the 'how'; it is first produced in Phase E and finalized and approved in Phase F.

questions.q: Which deliverable is the container for the core architectural artifacts and communicates the qualitative intent of the architecture?
questions.e: The Architecture Definition Document is the qualitative container for core architectural artifacts; it spans all four domains and examines baseline, transition, and target states.

questions.q: Why does TOGAF recommend considering architecture alternatives?
o: Because only one valid target architecture can ever exist
Because there may be multiple valid targets, and presenting alternatives surfaces hidden agendas, trade-offs, and new requirements
Because alternatives replace the need for principles
Because alternatives are mandated in Phase H only
questions.e: Multiple valid target architectures may conform to the vision, principles, and requirements; presenting alternatives builds understanding and surfaces trade-offs, hidden agendas, and new requirements.

questions.q: Who sets the priority and focus for the Architecture Capability's operating model?
questions.e: In the Architecture Capability operating model, the business sets priority and focus; the main goal is to develop, use, and sustain the target architecture to govern change.

questions.q: The Architecture Definition Document is first drafted in Phase A. When is it finalized?
questions.e: The ADD is first drafted in Phase A, enriched in Phases B, C, and D, and finalized in Phase F.
